label: Abandoned stilt village
glyph: brown tiered timber hall on stilts
meaning: An abandoned Argonian stilt village.
why: The nearest key glyph is Hammerfell's Ra Gada ruin, the native people's ruin; Black Marsh draws it as a tiered timber stilt hall, the Argonian way of building (story/lore/topics/material-culture.md). All eight lie in the south-centre round Blackrose and the Tulmek Washes.

label: Barsaebic Ayleid ruin
glyph: glowing white tree in a dark arch
meaning: A ruin of the Barsaebic Ayleids.
why: New to Black Marsh. Two of its six places carry canon Barsaebic names, Loriasel and Gandranen (Lore:Barsaebic Ayleids; story/lore/topics/lost-peoples.md), and all six lie in the north-west, the Barsaebics' land beside Blackwood; the glow is the welkynd light of Ayleid ruins.

label: Camp
glyph: yellow flame on a dark base
meaning: A camp: of a named Argonian tribe (Naga, Paatru, Sarpa, Tumnatu), or of pirates or smugglers.
why: The High Rock key's Camp glyph. The Naga, Paatru and Sarpa are canon Black Marsh tribes (story/lore/tribes.md); the labels name the occupants.

label: Cave
meaning: A natural cave.
why: The key's Cave glyph.

label: Keep
glyph: grey stone keep with a red banner
meaning: A stone keep (Fort Rustmoth, Fort Swiftmoth, Rainbreaker Keep).
why: New to Black Marsh. Two carry the '-moth' names of Imperial Legion forts (Morrowind's Fort Moonmoth, Hawkmoth, Buckmoth), and the map gives them an icon rather than a settlement glyph: a keep outside the living garrison network. Who holds each in 4E 201 is the research's call.

label: Imperial ruin
glyph: ochre tower face with two windows
pt_key_name: Second Empire ruin / Third Empire ruin
meaning: A ruined Imperial tower, waystation or fort of the Second or Third Empire.
why: The same glyph is the Second Empire ruin in Hammerfell's key and the Third Empire ruin in High Rock's: an Imperial ruin of either era. Black Marsh was an Imperial province until the Argonians drove the Empire out (story/lore/topics/history-timeline.md).

label: Kothringi ruin
meaning: A stone ruin of the Kothringi.
why: High Rock's key uses this glyph for the ruins of a foreign human people's strongholds; in Black Marsh all eight lie in the west around Gideon, where canon puts the Kothringi 'in large numbers' (story/lore/topics/lost-peoples.md). No Nord element is kept (decision 0006).

label: Landmark
meaning: A landmark; labelled [Peak] it is a high point.
why: The key's Landmark glyph.

label: Lilmothiit ruin
glyph: olive turf dome with a leafy crown
meaning: A den-village ruin of the Lilmothiit.
why: New to Black Marsh. All nine lie along the south and south-east coast, which canon says the Lilmothiit held before they died of the Knahaten Flu; nomadic fox-folk building in turf and leaf leave just such low domes (story/lore/topics/lost-peoples.md).

label: Mine
glyph: crossed pick with a lit torch
meaning: A mine.
why: The key's Mine glyph (Black Marsh adds a torch).

label: Shipwreck
glyph: listing hull and mast in water
meaning: A wreck (one, [Downed Bathysphere], is a sunken diving vessel).
why: The key's Shipwreck glyph.

label: Sunken ruin
glyph: dark green spire with curling arms, on open water
meaning: A drowned spire on the sea floor.
why: New to Black Marsh. All seven stand in open sea off the south-east, in Benthic Yobesh by Bell Station, Echo Deep and a [Downed Bathysphere]: places of diving and the deep. Who built them is the research's call.

label: Cantemiric Velothi ruin
meaning: A ruin of the Cantemiric Velothi.
why: New to Black Marsh. All twelve lie on the eastern seaboard between Archon, Arnesia and Thorn, where canon puts the Cantemiric Velothi, Dunmer settlers dead of the Knahaten Flu (story/lore/topics/lost-peoples.md); the stepped dome is a Velothi shrine form.

label: Large city
meaning: A major city.
why: The key's tier glyph, unchanged.

label: Metropolis
meaning: A great city and seat of power.
why: The key's tier glyph, unchanged (the owner: tiers are the same on both maps).

label: Minor location
meaning: A farm, homestead, logging camp, quarry, ferry, lighthouse or small post; the label says which.
why: The key's tier glyph, unchanged.

label: Outpost, fortress or important camp
meaning: A fort, waystation, hamlet or permanent camp; the label and the research say which.
why: The key's tier glyph, unchanged.

label: Small city
meaning: A regional city.
why: The key's tier glyph, unchanged.

label: Small city, seat
glyph: hexagon inside a second hexagon or ring
meaning: A regional city that is the seat of its culture's chief.
why: The map rings a few glyphs inside their tier (Tsonac, Aroxhu), as the key rings the Metropolis glyph itself: we read the ring as a seat of rule. Inferred, not stated.

label: Town
meaning: A market town.
why: The key's tier glyph, unchanged.

label: Town, seat
meaning: A town that is the seat of its culture's chief.
why: As the small-city seat: one ringed town per culture (Jal-Veesa, Yulca, Korydon, Uluo).

label: Village
meaning: A village.
why: The key's tier glyph, unchanged.

label: Village, seat
meaning: A village that is the seat of its culture's chief (Seafalls, the only village of its own culture).
why: As the small-city seat.
